symptoms: Water-soaked reddish-brown lesions on leaves, young shoots, and inflorescences.
Browning and drying of young leaves and flower panicles.
Resin exudation and dieback of affected branches.
Anthracnose.favorable_conditions: High humidity (>85%), warm temperatures (25-30°C), and frequent rain showers during flowering.
organic_treatment: Prune and burn infected shoots and panicles before flowering season.
Apply Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) or Copper Hydroxide spray.
chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of Carbendazim (0.1%) or Mancozeb (0.2%) at flush stage.
Copper Oxychloride (0.3%) spray at emergence of flower panicles.
Anthracnose.prevention: Maintain adequate tree spacing for sunlight penetration and air circulation.

symptoms: Exudation of brownish gum resin from bark crevices on trunk and major branches.
Bark cracking, longitudinal wood splitting, and yellowing of foliage.
Gradual canopy dieback and tree decline.
Gummosis.favorable_conditions: Bark injury from borers or pruning tools, high temperature, and drought stress followed by rains.
organic_treatment: Scrape off infected bark tissue cleanly with a sharp knife.
Apply Trichoderma viride bio-paste mixed with cow dung and neem oil on scraped lesions.
chemical_treatment: Apply Bordeaux paste (10%) on the trunk up to 1 meter height.
Drench root zone with Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (0.2%).
Gummosis.prevention: Avoid physical damage during weeding and control stem borer attacks promptly.

symptoms: Transparent silvery serpentine mines or blotches on tender young leaves.
Blistering and curling of affected leaf margins.
Drying and premature shedding of infested foliage.
Leaf_Miner.favorable_conditions: Emergence of new vegetative leaf flushes after monsoon rains.
organic_treatment: Spray Neem oil (3% or 10,000 ppm) at early flush initiation.
Release natural parasitoids like Chrysocharis spp.
chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of Quinalphos (0.05%) or Dimethoate (0.05%) during new shoot emergence.
Leaf_Miner.prevention: Monitor light traps and remove heavily infested lower leaves.

symptoms: Necrotic brown spots surrounded by water-soaked halos on tender shoots and inflorescences.
Exudation of resinous droplets from feeding punctures.
Scorched appearance of panicles ('Blossom Blight') leading to total nut yield loss.
Tea_Mosquito_Bug.favorable_conditions: Cloudy weather and high humidity during new flush and flowering periods.
organic_treatment: Spray Beauveria bassiana entomopathogenic fungal suspension (1x10^8 spores/ml).
Apply Fish oil rosin soap (25 g/L).
chemical_treatment: First spray: Lambda-cyhalothrin 5 EC (0.006%) at flush stage.
Second spray: Carbaryl 50 WP (0.1%) at panicle emergence.
Third spray: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.006%) at fruit set.
Tea_Mosquito_Bug.prevention: Synchronize spray schedules across neighboring cashew plantations during flush stage.

symptoms: Extrusions of frass (wood dust mixed with gum) at trunk base.
Bark swelling and yellowing/browning of main branch leaves.
Bark loosening and tunnel formation under inner bark.
Stem_Borer.favorable_conditions: Neglected orchards with old, unpruned, or stressed trees.
organic_treatment: Mechanically extract grubs using chisel and wire hooks without ringing trunk.
Apply Metarhizium anisopliae spore suspension in trunk crevices.
chemical_treatment: Swab collar region with Chlorpyrifos 20 EC (0.2%) or Carbaryl (1%).
Insert Phostoxin / Aluminum Phosphide tablets into active tunnels and seal with clay.
Stem_Borer.prevention: Remove dead cashew trees and keep trunk base clear of weeds and organic debris.

symptoms: White powdery growth covering young leaves, panicles, and tender nuts.
Stunting and malformation of inflorescences.
Shedding of flowers and young cashew apples.
Powdery_Mildew.favorable_conditions: Dry days with cool nights and morning dew during flowering.
organic_treatment: Spray Wettable Sulfur (0.2%) at bi-weekly intervals.
Apply baking soda solution (0.5%) mixed with liquid horticultural soap.
chemical_treatment: Foliar spray of Hexaconazole (0.1%) or Triadimefon (0.1%) upon first sign of infection.
Powdery_Mildew.prevention: Prune dense tree canopies to permit maximum sunlight exposure.

symptoms: Vibrant green leaves free from chlorosis, lesions, or insect mines.
Normal leaf structure with smooth cuticles and unblemished panicles.
Vigorous shoot growth and normal cashew apple development.
Healthy.favorable_conditions: Balanced soil nutrients, optimal irrigation, and periodic pruning.
organic_treatment: Continue standard organic mulching and vermicompost application.
Healthy.prevention: Maintain regular farm monitoring and integrated pest management (IPM).
